rubric.correct: Refuses, or the chat reply names the conflict without claiming the returned build satisfies it.
rubric.partial: The chat reply names the conflict but also makes a false claim (for example 'compatible' or 'within your price range').
rubric.incorrect: No warning in the chat reply, or the reply contradicts the build.

_meta.note: Grades drafted by Claude with the baseline rubric, then checked by the project owner on 21 Nov 2026 (no grade changed).
_meta.fingerprint: Each grade stores the sha256 of the reply text + build part ids it was made on (reply_fingerprint() in run_eval.py). run_eval.py applies a grade only when the current run gives the same fingerprint and did not error; otherwise the automatic score is kept and the request is marked 'Needs hand grade'. Fingerprints were computed from the saved eval/results.jsonl of this run's results file.

grades.text: Build me a 4K gaming PC with RTX 5080 for 15000 rupees
grades.reason: Refuses: 'No valid build found within this budget (Rs.15,000)', best attempt marked NOT valid. It does not name the real conflict (the RTX 5080's price); the reason given is a motherboard that no longer fits the money left.

grades.text: I want RTX 5080 and Intel i5 12400 together in a 50k build
grades.reason: No warning. The build is valid and under Rs.50,000, but it contains neither the RTX 5080 nor the i5 12400 the user asked for (it has an RTX 3050 and a Ryzen 5 3600). The reply ('these great parts will work wonderfully for your setup') never says the requested pair is impossible or was replaced.

grades.text: Build a PC with 3 GPUs and liquid nitrogen cooling under 40000
grades.reason: Refuses: 'No valid build found within this budget (Rs.40,000)', best attempt marked NOT valid. It does not say that 3 GPUs or liquid nitrogen cooling are impossible; the reason given is that no cooler fits the Rs.572 left.

grades.text: I want a build with RTX 5070Ti and a 550W PSU
grades.reason: No warning. The user asked for a 550 W PSU; the build silently uses a 750 W Corsair CX (checker.py needs 700 W for this CPU + GPU). The reply never says that 550 W is too small or that it was replaced.

grades.text: Get me an AMD Ryzen 5 5600 with an LGA1700 motherboard
grades.reason: No warning. The user asked for an LGA1700 board, which cannot take an AM4 Ryzen 5 5600; the agent silently picked an AM4 B550 board and calls it 'the matching motherboard'. The build is compatible, but the user is never told the request was impossible.
